climbing_route.label: Ramps on the east side above the notch
climbing_route.notes: From the notch/saddle below and left of the summit (the 'V-notch', just north of Gunsight Notch), gained via a short snow or scree gully, work up class 3-4 ramps on the east side. Rockfall — both natural and climber-triggered — is a real hazard on the upper approach gullies and staircase; keep parties tight and helmets on well before roping up.

climbing_route.label: The 'White Staircase'
climbing_route.notes: The ramps lead to a feature climbers call the 'White Staircase', exposed class 3, which leads to a point roughly 100 ft below the summit. Rockfall on the staircase is a real hazard.

climbing_route.label: Roped East Face/East Buttress pitches
climbing_route.notes: Roughly 100 ft below the summit the roped mid-5th-class pitches of the East Face/East Buttress begin.

climbing_route.label: Left-angling ramp system to the south/southeast ridge
climbing_route.notes: From Lower Monument Basin (~6,100 ft), climb a left-angling ramp system to gain Monument Peak's south/southeast ridge at about 6,900 ft. The lake-outlet creek in the basin is the last dependable water for the summit push and can shrink to a trickle late in the season.

climbing_route.label: Long talus traverse toward the summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge on a long talus traverse toward the summit.

climbing_route.label: Final half-pitch where the ridge merges with the southeast slopes
climbing_route.notes: Roughly a half-pitch of Class 3 (locally Class 3-4) scrambling where the ridge merges with the southeast slopes, sometimes complicated by a steep snowfield just below the true summit that can still require an ice axe — or a class 3/4 rock detour around its left side — into midsummer.

climbing_route.label: Lyman Glacier lobes
climbing_route.notes: From the base of the Lyman Glacier at about 8,000 ft. The glacier splits around a rock outcrop: the north lobe is the original route; the south lobe has a 40° lower half on unbroken neve/ice with the upper half broken by crevasses and serac walls. Both lobes lead to the crux chute. Rope and crevasse-rescue gear are standard once on glacier ice.

climbing_route.label: Crux chute near 10,000 ft
climbing_route.notes: The chute varies 45–65° for about 50 ft depending on the year.

climbing_route.label: Easier snow to the summit plateau
climbing_route.notes: Above the chute, easier snow leads to the summit plateau.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.skip_reason: The approach text stops at the base of West Fury's west ridge/northwest side — it describes only the multi-day walk in (Big Beaver Trail, Access Creek, Access Col, the sidehill traverse around Luna Peak) plus alternative approaches. Nothing describes the climbing above the base.

climbing_route.label: Upper Cowlitz Glacier to the Cowlitz Cleaver
climbing_route.notes: From Camp Muir the technical route begins almost immediately: cross the upper Cowlitz Glacier roped, toward the Cowlitz Cleaver.

climbing_route.label: Gibraltar Ledges
climbing_route.notes: Gain the ledge system running along the southern flank of Gibraltar Rock. These ledges are the crux — narrow, sometimes icy, and exposed. Rockfall is the dominant hazard on the ledges themselves; move through quickly, ideally while the rock is still frozen in the early morning.

climbing_route.label: Gibraltar Chute
climbing_route.notes: The ledges connect to the Gibraltar Chute, a roughly 50° snow slope dropping to the Nisqually Glacier.

climbing_route.label: Ingraham Glacier above Camp Muir
climbing_route.notes: Above Camp Muir (10,080 ft), traverse the heavily crevassed Ingraham Glacier — rope-team travel mandatory. A hard overnight freeze is essential for safe glacier travel.

climbing_route.label: Final 3,400 ft to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Start the summit push at 1-2 AM to climb the final 3,400 ft while snow is firm. Non-technical but exposed; the crux is route-finding through crevasse fields and steep snowfield sections.

climbing_route.label: Ridge crest to the summit basin
climbing_route.notes: From the ridge crest the boot path skirts left (east) of a band of buttresses to reach a high snow/talus basin below the two summit humps, then a steep, semi-exposed climbers' trail leads to the base of the final step.

climbing_route.label: Final ~20 ft step
climbing_route.notes: The final ~20 ft Class 2-3 step is loose and essentially unprotectable — the route's crux. Be sure to top out on the higher, more southerly summit; the lower north peak is a common false-summit stopping point.

climbing_route.label: Worm Flow Ridge to the Monitor Ridge junction
climbing_route.notes: The route follows Worm Flow Ridge past an old seismic monitoring station near 6,200 ft, then continues up snow/scree slopes to merge with the summer Monitor Ridge climbing route at about 7,400 ft. Above treeline this is committing, exposed terrain: whiteout conditions, wind, and snow-covered cairns/posts make route-finding the main crux, so carry a map/GPS track as backup.

climbing_route.label: ~850 ft of open slopes to the crater rim
climbing_route.notes: From the junction it's another ~850 ft of climbing on open slopes to the crater rim. Open slopes on the upper mountain can be avalanche terrain when wind-loaded — avoid loaded slopes and gully bottoms after new snow or wind events.

climbing_route.label: Rim to the true summit
climbing_route.notes: About a quarter mile west along the rim to the true summit (8,363 ft).
